arxiv-2104-09089.title: Generalization of a density theorem of Khinchin and diophantine approximation
arxiv-2104-09089.creator: J. Beck, W.W.L. Chen
arxiv-2104-09089.description: Abstract . The continuous version of a fundamental result of Khinchin says that a half-infinite torus line in the unit square [ 0 , 1 ] 2 [0,1]^{2} exhibits superdensity, which is a best form of time-quantitative density, if and only if the slope of the geodesic is a badly approximable number.

arxiv-2209-14805.title: Estimation of Electrical Characteristics of Inhomogeneous Walls Using Generative Adversarial Networks
arxiv-2209-14805.creator: Kainat Yasmeen, Shobha Sundar Ram
arxiv-2209-14805.description: Abstract Through-wall radars are researched and developed for the detection, localization, and tracking of human activities in indoor environments. Electromagnetic wave propagation through walls introduces refraction, attenuation, multipath, and ghost targets in the radar signatures. Estimation of wall characteristics (dielectric profile and thickness) can enable wall effects to be deconvolved from through-wall radar signatures.

arxiv-2301-10776.title: T − T- linear resistivity from magneto-elastic scattering: application to PdCrO 2
arxiv-2301-10776.creator: J.F. Mendez-Valderrama, Evyatar Tulipman, Elina Zhakina, Andrew P. Mackenzie, Erez Berg, Debanjan Chowdhury
arxiv-2301-10776.description: Abstract An electronic solid with itinerant carriers and localized magnetic moments represents a paradigmatic strongly correlated system. The electrical transport properties associated with the itinerant carriers, as they scatter off these local moments, has been scrutinized across a number of materials.

arxiv-2303-12497.title: Lower Bounds on the Bayesian Risk via Information Measures
arxiv-2303-12497.creator: Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Adrien Vandenbroucque, Michael Gastpar
arxiv-2303-12497.description: Abstract This paper focuses on parameter estimation and introduces a new method for lower bounding the Bayesian risk. The method allows for the use of virtually any information measure, including Rényi’s α \alpha , φ \varphi -Divergences, and Sibson’s α \alpha -Mutual Information.

arxiv-2411-00711.title: Debiasify : Self-Distillation for Unsupervised Bias Mitigation
arxiv-2411-00711.creator: Nourhan Bayasi, Jamil Fayyad, Ghassan Hamarneh, Rafeef Garbi, Homayoun Najjaran
arxiv-2411-00711.description: Abstract Simplicity bias is a critical challenge in neural networks since it often leads to favoring simpler solutions and learning unintended decision rules captured by spurious correlations, causing models to be biased and diminishing their generalizability. While existing solutions rely on human supervision, obtaining annotations of the different bias attributes is often impractical.

pmc-11490537.title: Evaluation of asphalt mixtures modified with low-density polyethylene and high-density polyethylene using experimental results and machine learning models
pmc-11490537.creator: Muhammad Junaid, Chaozhe Jiang, Uneb Gazder, Imran Hafeez, Diyar Khan
pmc-11490537.description: The widespread use of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE) plastics has resulted in a large amount of waste plastic that requires appropriate disposal or reuse. One potential solution is to use them in the modification of asphalt concrete (AC) mixtures for more sustainable highways.

pmc-12530610.title: Identification of dominant global and local modes behind dynamic stiffness valleys in BIW structures via modal contribution and ESE
pmc-12530610.creator: Mingsheng Wang, Wendi Wang, Tao Chen, Xiangwei Lu, Xuelian Yi
pmc-12530610.description: This study proposes a novel methodology that integrates modal contribution analysis with Element Strain Energy (ESE) distribution to identify the dominant modes causing dynamic stiffness variations in Body-in-White (BIW) structures. As Noise, Vibration, and Harshness (NVH) performance becomes increasingly critical in automotive design, accurately identifying the sources of dynamic stiffness deficiencies in the early design stages is imperative.

pmc-12550313.title: Laying the groundwork for an inter-ministerial One Health response to antimicrobial resistance in South Korea
pmc-12550313.creator: Seok Hyeon Na, Inji Jun, Sangrim Kang, Jung Sik Yoo, Eun-Jeong Yoon
pmc-12550313.description: BackgroundThe five-year project to address the threat of AMR, One Health Multi-Ministerial Project on AMR, was implemented in 2019 in South Korea with coordinating action across human, animal, environmental, and food sectors. To describe the design, implementation, and outcomes of the initiative, assess its contribution to AMR preparedness, and identify policy implications for sustaining progress.

pmc-12565331.title: Association of Bruxism with the Occurrence of Sleep Disorders and the Nature of Dreams
pmc-12565331.creator: Sandra Szostak, Aleksandra Karykowska, Halina Kołodziej, Maciej Dobrzynski, Ioannis Ilias, Athanassios Tselebis, Argyro Pachi
pmc-12565331.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Bruxism is defined as repetitive activity of the masticatory muscles characterized by clenching or grinding of the teeth and/or stiffening or protrusion of the mandible, referred to as sleep bruxism or awake bruxism. It is believed that in generally healthy individuals, bruxism should not be considered a disorder, but rather a behavior that may be a risk factor (and/or protective factor) for certain clinical consequences.

pmc-13271064.title: From overlooked to outstanding: a molecular silver complex in heterogeneous CO2 electroreduction
pmc-13271064.creator: Wiebke Wiesner, Kevinjeorjios Pellumbi, Julia Jökel, Ulf-Peter Apfel
pmc-13271064.description: Heterogenized molecular transition metal complexes, especially silver-based ones, have shown to be highly efficient as catalysts for electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R). Herein we present the application of a silver dithiacyclam polymer (dithiacyclam = 1,8-dithia-4,11-diazacyclotetradecane, Ag(dithiacyclam)) in homogeneous as well as heterogeneous eCO2R.

pmc-13314714.title: Challenges in Diagnosis and Management of Crohn's Disease in Bangladesh With Long Term Follow‐Up
pmc-13314714.creator: Imtiaz Abdullah, Imran Hasan, Mantaka Rahman, Shoma Hayat, Nowshin Papri, Nusrat Fatema, Ahmedul Kabir, Zhahirul Islam
pmc-13314714.description: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) with significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We reported a case of a 20‐year‐old Bangladeshi male with an 8‐month history of severe upper abdominal pain, bowel discomfort, and intermittent low‐grade fever. Initial investigations showed mild anemia and elevated inflammatory markers.

pmc-13358220.title: Identification and Genomic Analysis of the First Salmonella typhimurium Monophasic Variant 1,4,[5],12:i:‐ Isolate Harbouring a Chromosomally Integrated bla NDM‐5
pmc-13358220.creator: Shihan Zeng, Weilong Guo, Chengfeng Lin, Lianghui Peng, Jingjie Song
pmc-13358220.description: We report the first clinical strain of the monophasic variant of Salmonella typhimurium (serotype 1,4,[5],12:i:‐) belonging to ST34 with chromosomally integrated bla NDM‐5. Although chromosomal integration of bla NDM‐5 has been described in other Enterobacterales and Salmonella serovars, this is the first such report in this high‐risk clone. This study characterises the genomic and epidemiological background of this strain.

pmc-13494957.title: Alcohol impacts an fMRI marker of neural inhibition in humans and rodents
pmc-13494957.creator: Monami Nishio, Xinyi Wang, Eli J. Cornblath, Sung-Ho Lee, Yen-Yu Ian Shih, Nicola Palomero-Gallagher, Michael J. Arcaro, David M. Lydon-Staley, Allyson P. Mackey
pmc-13494957.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Inhibitory neuronal activity is a key regulator of brain function and is implicated in numerous developmental and psychiatric disorders. However, measuring inhibition in vivo remains a challenge. The Hurst exponent of the fMRI signal has been shown to correlate spatially with cellular measures of neural inhibition, but there have been few causal tests of the relationship between the Hurst exponent and neural inhibition.
